items.html:
I recommend one release/0.1.0 integration branch, based on sanitized, rewritten history, with fewer than 100 commits. The main development work is largely complete, but threading, framework correctness, release integration, and privacy cleanup still need work.

Your clarified requirements are incorporated: remove incidental PII throughout code, documentation, benchmarks, archives, and retained history; preserve authorship, citations, license attribution, and functional project URLs.

The nine branches resolve into four implementation sources and temporary coordination branches.

Branch Audited tip Proposed disposition
claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh 1f8b6077 (condensed into 8251007) Main implementation baseline. Contains 1,536 commits.
claude/r4-python ec51a182 (condensed into 8251007) Already fully included in improvements; retire afterward.
claude/r4-docs 5d3d8777 (condensed into 8251007) Already fully included in improvements; retire afterward.
claude/framework-adapter-fixes 50058abd (condensed into ae22657) Integrate its three additional commits after completing the fixes below.
claude/treams-rs-multithreading-hardware-na6nrm 9e98d507 (condensed into ae22657) Finish four additional commits and two embedded patches, then integrate.
claude/release-readiness bf088769 Port its 56 additional commits into the refactored implementation.
r4-tooling ea896293 Preserve privately; never merge into the product.
r4-tooling-python 79e3e0ad Fully included in r4-tooling; retire.
r4-tooling-docs 22fd81a6 Fully included in r4-tooling; retire.

All 105 round-4 work packages are recorded as merged, with no missing package IDs. The release branch remains substantially unreconciled. The threading branch has already been rebuilt on the round-4 baseline; the release handoff’s statement that it still uses the old layout is stale.

I also found three experimental branches—browser, GPU, and Aeneas. I recommend preserving them privately and excluding them from this first release.

This is the work I propose completing before the integration branch is ready.

  1. Sanitize the complete retained history and benchmark evidence.

    This goes beyond replacing paths in the final checkout. Historical main contains personal paths, a private hostname/network address, and earlier unsanitized scripts and benchmark records.

    All five benchmark archive payloads also contain personal owner/group metadata: 15,200 archive members in total. Three additionally contain personal paths inside logs or captured agent material:

    • agent-api-20260920/evidence.tar.gz
    • agent-api-20260920/review-evidence.tar.gz
    • linux-core-performance-20260919.tar.gz
    • linux-core-qualification-20260919.tar.gz
    • The split linux-qualification-report-20260920.tar.gz.part-* archive

    I would preserve original evidence privately, redact incidental identities in public copies, normalize archive ownership metadata, and update affected checksums and manifests. Numerical arrays, timings, scores, tolerances, hardware specifications, and scientific results must remain unchanged and be compared against the originals.

    Public evidence should explicitly identify privacy-only sanitization. Original measurement revisions must remain distinguishable from rewritten revisions; changing a commit hash must never imply that a benchmark was rerun.

  2. Condense and correct the Git history.

    Across the fetched refs there are 1,810 distinct commits, including 1,728 authored and committed by Claude. Existing main has 79 commits, already attributed correctly.

    My proposed approach is to sanitize the retained main lineage, then reconstruct the development delta as approximately 10–15 coherent commits. That gives roughly 89–94 commits, with a hard ceiling of 100 including integration overhead. We can condense further where historical snapshots add little value.

    All reconstructed development commits would use:

    [name] <[e-mail address]>

    Both author and committer fields need checking. Claude coauthor/session trailers should disappear from the reconstructed messages. Old development and tooling branches must not remain reachable from the public repository.

    Before rewriting, preserve a private recovery copy and freeze branch writers. Afterward, verify every retained ref and prevent an old branch from reintroducing the original history.

  3. Finish the threading implementation.

    Two substantial changes exist only as files under handoff/: allocation-error handling and ordered pullback reductions. They are not applied to the branch’s production code.

    The branch records a Clippy failure, an expected reproducibility-test failure, stale generated documentation, and missing full Python/wheel verification. Both patches reportedly passed Rust checks together, but that does not qualify the integrated package. (Threading handoff)

    Required completion includes:

    • Apply and review both patches.
    • Verify gradients across thread counts and repeated calls.
    • Exercise fork, spawn, and forkserver after native parallel work.
    • Verify thread controls, context restoration, threadpoolctl, ufunc operations, and floating-point modes.
    • Check peak memory: ordered reductions can retain many partial gradients.
    • Complete consequential allocation-error paths or narrow the documented MemoryError guarantee to actual coverage.

    Sequential SVD/eigendecomposition and the current scheduling thresholds can stay. Further parallel optimization is not required for this release.

  4. Complete the framework fixes and close two confirmed validation gaps.

    Coincident particles: NumPy Cluster.solve() rejects them, but factor() and scatter() bypass that validation and can return a finite, physically invalid response. The framework branch fixes only its own scattering route. Enforce the geometry requirement consistently without breaking legitimate self-block handling in generic expansion. (Cluster implementation)

    Chiral port waves: PortWave.with_polarization("parity") bypasses the new achirality checks. A wave in a chiral exterior can therefore enter an unsupported polarization representation and evaluate fields. Cover static and traced chirality through Advect, JAX, and Torch. (Port-wave conversion)

    Also finish full framework verification, repair the benchmark’s Torch detach warning and worker cleanup, and obtain trustworthy before/after measurements.

  5. Resolve the outstanding numerical behavior questions explicitly.

    These are documented limitations or handoff reports; I did not reproduce their numerical examples during this audit.

    Issue Proposed treatment
    Partial-polarization slabs use different projection semantics in NumPy and framework APIs. Reproduce the discrepancy and establish one supported behavior, or reject the unsupported construction.
    Gain media/strong chirality reportedly produce order-one differences between interface implementations. Compare against an independent reference; fix or explicitly constrain support.
    Negative-real spherical Ewald wavenumbers can return the wrong branch of the function. Reject the unsupported spherical Ewald domain centrally, preserving supported cylindrical/direct-shell inputs.
    Some gain-media lattice results depend on the split despite broader independence claims. Align accepted inputs and documentation with demonstrated behavior.
    An extreme spherical-field case produces NaN through dimension-dependent intermediate scaling. Test equivalent physical problems in different units; correct scaling or fail clearly outside supported limits.

    These should receive bounded investigations. Existing documented limits—CPU execution, first-order differentiation, singular thresholds, conditioning limits, and unsupported fractional-complex functions—do not require new general-purpose implementations.

    The accepted (V^{1/3}) automatic 3D Ewald split and accepted multi-origin expansion behavior should remain; they are settled decisions.

  6. Port the release branch’s numerical, dependency, and licensing changes.

    Keep the refactored module structure. Port the clean-room Legendre/Ferrers implementation into special/ferrers.rs, preserving its provenance constraint and regression coverage. The saved draft port is not a finished integration.

    Also port the spherical-polar property-test correction, reconcile dependencies and tool versions, and regenerate license bundles against the final lockfiles. Remove current XSF-derived attribution only once the replacement is actually integrated; preserve all applicable upstream and bundled dependency attribution.

    The recorded release target is already 0.1.0, CPython 3.12–3.15, MIT project licensing, and no conda release. (Release decisions and port checklist)

  7. Reconcile CI and packaging without losing existing coverage.

    Keep the release branch’s intended 20 wheels plus sdist: four Python versions across Linux x86-64/ARM64, macOS Intel/ARM64, and Windows x86-64.

    Specific integration repairs are needed:

    • Update wheel smoke tests that call removed or renamed APIs.
    • Preserve the optimized installed-wheel floating-point-environment checks.
    • Separate ordinary test helpers from unconditional upstream treams imports. Otherwise newer-Python collection either fails or skips unrelated tests.
    • Preserve the CI Hypothesis profile: selecting the release workflow unchanged would reduce coverage from 100 to 30 examples.
    • Reconcile test categories, moved paths, generators, formal checks, and the authoritative verification command.
    • Verify dependency floors/latest versions and explicitly account for accepted newer-Python oracle exclusions.
    • Add the small missing __version__ and CLI program-name fixes.

    A draft integration PR can exercise the complete nonpublishing wheel workflow. Publishing machinery does not need to be merged first merely to test distributions.

  8. Finish the public documentation and repair Pages publication.

    Keep the round-4 Material site, generated reference, examples, and navigation. Add the agreed versioned dev, 0.1.0, and latest documentation with rustdoc in each version.

    There is a concrete deployment defect: the release workflow pushes Mike output using GITHUB_TOKEN, while its instructions configure branch-based Pages publishing. GitHub states that those pushes do not trigger Pages builds. Use explicit Pages artifact deployment for the complete versioned site. (Workflow), GitHub behavior

    Also:

    • Consolidate the contradictory release instructions into one procedure.
    • Update installation, platform support, optional extras, and source-build instructions.
    • Fix versioned deep links and source links for corrected release documentation.
    • Retain current tested API examples rather than restoring older release-branch examples.
    • Distinguish the current test oracle from historical 0.4.5 benchmark evidence.
    • Condense the 741-line changelog into coherent first-release notes while retaining the useful API name mapping.
    • Update citation version/date and supported security-version information.
    • Regenerate and execute examples, then visually inspect the rendered site.

  9. Give the remaining performance results a clear disposition.

    The final round-4 rerun still records eight results above its 3% slowdown threshold:

    Measurement Recorded slowdown
    Power transmittance/reflectance backward 16.5%
    Plane operator backward 11.7%
    Oriented chirality backward 7.3%
    Legendre forward 6.1%
    Cube enumeration 5.6%
    Angular pi forward 4.0%
    Cylindrical particle cluster backward 4.0%
    Wigner backward 3.7%

    Earlier work explicitly stopped investigating these. The framework branch separately reports noisy small-Advect-parity slowdowns of 15–27%.

    I recommend one bounded comparison on an idle host after integration stabilizes: these cases, changed framework calls, unchanged controls, and representative threading memory measurements. Then fix established regressions or record explicit accepted exceptions. Historical speedups against upstream do not establish absence of regressions against treams-rs itself. (Recorded final rerun)

  10. Remove temporary material and complete hosted release setup.

Remove completed HANDOFF.md files, handoff/, embedded patches, the abandoned custom documentation theme and checks, obsolete generators, and duplicate PR/release instructions. Retire all superseded branches after preserving their useful work privately.

Keep scientific evidence, reference tables, supported compatibility aliases, and useful evaluation tooling, subject to sanitization. I found no justification for broadly deleting those assets. The nine untracked benchmark/report paths in the current checkout also need archive-equivalence checks before cleanup.

Live GitHub state currently shows:

  • Private repository; no PRs, releases, tags, or forks.
  • Unprotected main; no rulesets.
  • pypi and testpypi environments restricted to main.
  • Missing separate release approval environment.
  • No Pages site or repository Actions variables.
  • 72 historical Actions runs and eight artifacts requiring privacy treatment.

Configure release approval, version-tag protection, Pages, Codecov, private vulnerability reporting, and verify both trusted-publisher registrations. First publication can use pending publishers. PyPI documentation

GitHub can retain old commits in cached views after a force-push. Hosted cleanup therefore needs verification before publication. If an in-place rewrite cannot satisfy the PII requirement, the alternative is to retain the existing repository privately and publish only sanitized history through a fresh repository at the intended URL. That repository migration would be a separate concrete decision. GitHub history-removal guidance

The completion sequence would be: preserve originals → reconcile and finish code → sanitize and condense history → qualify the final integration revision → review → merge → run exact-main CI and the release procedure.

The integration should arrive at review with passing Rust/Python/formal checks, complete wheel/sdist builds, installed-package checks, rendered documentation review, resolved numerical/performance dispositions, and a privacy audit of every retained revision and distributable. After merging, the publisher requires successful push CI for the resulting main SHA; earlier branch results cannot substitute for that.

I would keep new GPU/browser work, additional Aeneas proofs, parallel decomposition optimization, new convenience APIs, and filing the SciPy report outside this release’s required scope.

Verification boundary: this was source, history, archive, tracker, and hosted-configuration inspection. No builds, tests, numerical reruns, or rendering were performed, and the privacy inspection is not yet exhaustive. Only local remote-tracking refs were refreshed; no source edits, commits, pushes, branch deletions, PRs, comments, or publication changes were made.
